# Open choices: test-design

`aidd-team:test-design` leaves these decisions to the team. aidd's default holds until a `standards` entry fills one. `aidd standard list` names the library standards for each choice, and `aidd standard add` adopts one.

| Choice | Question | aidd's default | Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `integration-test-services` | How does an integration test start the databases and services it needs? | Testcontainers where the ecosystem has a library for it, one throwaway container per test run. | Testcontainers, Docker Compose started by the test run, the provider's local emulator |
| `coverage-tool` | Which tool measures the coverage of the tests in CI, and which floor fails the run? | The test runner's own coverage report in CI, with two checks. A line floor, set to today's coverage when the check is added and raised as coverage rises, never lowered. And the lines each change adds or touches covered at 80% or more, through the tool's diff report. Coverage shows the code no test ran; the Mutation run judges how strong the tests are. | coverage.py, Vitest coverage, cargo-llvm-cov, JaCoCo, go test -cover, no coverage floor |
| `fuzzer` | Which fuzzer runs the Parser fuzzing of `aidd-team:secure-coding`, and how does CI keep what it finds? | libFuzzer through the language's own harness, fuzzing each parser for a set time on a schedule, with every crash input kept and replayed as a regression test. | libFuzzer, AFL++, Jazzer, Go native fuzzing, Atheris |
| `undefined-behavior-check` | Which check finds undefined behaviour in unsafe code, or in code in a memory-unsafe language? | The compiler's sanitizers, AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, over the test suite in CI, wherever the code can break memory safety. | AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, Miri, Valgrind |
